newsitem.title: USA: Coastal, Transco enter Ohio-Pa. gas line venture.
newsitem.headline: Coastal, Transco enter Ohio-Pa. gas line venture.

text.p: Coastal Corp's ANR Pipeline Co (ANR) and Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Corp (Transco) said Monday they had agreed to form a joint venture, called Independence Pipeline Co, to build a natural gas pipeline from Ohio to Pennsylvania.

The 36-inch diameter line, with an initial capacity of 900 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd), will run 370 miles from ANR's compressor station in Defiance, Ohio, to Transco's facilities at Leidy, Pa, ANR said in a statement.
"Affiliates of ANR and Transco will each own 50 percent of the new project," the statement said, adding "The final cost of the project has not been determined."
The project is tentatively scheduled to start service in November, 1999, pending approval by, among others, the Washington-based Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC).

The line aims to relieve bottlenecks currently seen in the Midwest gas transportation network, a problem that is likely to grow as new pipelines are poised to bring more gas into the region from Canada and U.S. gas fields farther west.

"Independence will link the very active Midwest gas market with the capacity-constrained eastern United States," Jeffrey Connelley, Coastal Corp's senior vice president for natural gas, said in prepared comments.
"The linkage of the ANR and Transco systems will provide gas producers and marketers with access to virtually every major market in the eastern half of the United States," he said.
ANR operates an interstate gas pipeline network of about 10,400 miles.
Transco, a subsidiary of Williams Companies, operates a 10,000-mile gas pipeline system spanning from the U.S. Gulf to New York.
